If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum). Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. THE EXPLORATORY TOPIC BRAINS is an Exploratory Topic with two (2) intake groups, each will take 18 months from kickoff to completion and will consist of two (2) 9-month phases with a down select at the end of Phase 1. Criteria for moving to Phase 2 are the metrics as described in Tables 2, 3, and 4 for Phase 1. 2.1 Technical Areas (TAs) and Milestones Using natural brain development as a blueprint, BRAINS will seed efforts for two (2) technical areas, which are essential for later steps in functionally replacing damaged brain tissue. In TA1 teams will design developmental mim icking or tissue engineering methods capable of generating precursor tissue for a part of the brain other than neocortex . In TA2 teams will provide proof-of-concept for surgical engraftment into adult brains of non -human fetal precursor tissues for their selected brain area. Teams must propose to address all milestones and metrics of either one TA or both. TA1: Defining and generating precursor tissue

Under this CSO, the DoD may seek solution briefs, presentations/pitches, and/or proposals from traditional and nontraditional business entities for innovative commercial products, technologies, and services, or adaptations/modifications of existing commercial products, technologies, and services to meet U.S. Army needs and improve readiness. These include, but are not limited to, IT modernization, enhanced cybersecurity, efficient artifact restoration and conservation, streamlined base operations, and improved facility support. This CSO may result in the award of various types of contracts, which may include, but are not limited to, commercially-available products, technologies, or services immediately available; commercially-available products, technologies, or services fueled by commercial or strategic investment; and concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile development activities that can incrementally improve commercial products, technologies, or services, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for broad defense applications. ars have been reserved for awards under this CSO. The participating DoD agencies will provide no funding for direct reimbursement of white paper or proposal development costs. NOTE: During any step of the CSO, the Government may send written questions or comments for companies to address via email, or other suitable communication methods as determined by the Government. Benefits of the CSO process and the potential for award include: A streamlined application process requiring only minimal corporate and technical information for fast-track evaluation timelines for solution briefs. Negotiable payment terms for non-dilutive capital. Negotiable intellectual property (IP) rights. Secure and direct feedback from end users, mission partners, and users within the DoD to help product teams develop and hone product design and functionality. CAV RP registration requires the contractor to purchase a commercial PKI certificate, complete web-based information assurance training (approximately 1 hour to complete) and submit a System Authorization Access Request (SAAR). THE EXPLORATORY TOPIC BRAINS is an Exploratory Topic with two (2) intake groups, each will take 18 months from kickoff to completion and will consist of two (2) 9-month phases with a down select at the end of Phase 1. Criteria for moving to Phase 2 are the metrics as described in Tables 2, 3, and 4 for Phase 1. 2.1 Technical Areas (TAs) and Milestones Using natural brain development as a blueprint, BRAINS will seed efforts for two (2) technical areas, which are essential for later steps in functionally replacing damaged brain tissue. In TA1 teams will design developmental mim icking or tissue engineering methods capable of generating precursor tissue for a part of the brain other than neocortex . In TA2 teams will provide proof-of-concept for surgical engraftment into adult brains of non -human fetal precursor tissues for their selected brain area. Teams must propose to address all milestones and metrics of either one TA or both. TA1: Defining and generating precursor tissue

The CSO authority is Section 803 of the National Defense Authorization Act for FY2022, Public Law 117-807, and Class Deviation 2022-O0007. 1.2 AoI Background CAA has a mission to conduct analyses of Army forces and systems in the context of joint and combined operations for key leaders at Headquarters, Department of the Army (HQDA) G-8 and Combined and Unified Commands. CAA’s Data Management Program performs an important role in meeting mission requirements in support of its 150 assigned personnel. CAA’s mission depends on the availability and integrity of authoritative data that requires the effective lifecycle management of both CAA’s supporting data and published work products. Under this CSO, the DoD may seek solution briefs, presentations/pitches, and/or proposals from traditional and nontraditional business entities for innovative commercial products, technologies, and services, or adaptations/modifications of existing commercial products, technologies, and services to meet U.S. Army needs and improve readiness. These include, but are not limited to, IT modernization, enhanced cybersecurity, efficient artifact restoration and conservation, streamlined base operations, and improved facility support. This CSO may result in the award of various types of contracts, which may include, but are not limited to, commercially-available products, technologies, or services immediately available; commercially-available products, technologies, or services fueled by commercial or strategic investment; and concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile development activities that can incrementally improve commercial products, technologies, or services, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for broad defense applications. Benefits of the CSO process and the potential for award include: A streamlined application process requiring only minimal corporate and technical information for fast-track evaluation timelines for solution briefs. Negotiable payment terms for non-dilutive capital. Negotiable intellectual property (IP) rights.
